title: Machine-enforced PR diff reuse gate with parallel task approvals

scope.subject: Repository-wide reuse policy enforcement across GitHub PRs and parallel agents

research_summary: Upgrade the existing Node reuse gate from a dirty-working-tree check into a GitHub PR-diff policy engine that can verify changed protected files against task-scoped approvals, while preserving the lightweight local gate and avoiding a second generic policy runtime.

sources.finding: GitHub Actions provides clean-runner pull-request execution and exposes base/head commit context suitable for deterministic diff gating.
Required status checks can make a named machine gate a merge prerequisite, preventing a missing or failing check from being treated as success.
OPA is a mature generic policy engine, but adopting Rego and another runtime would duplicate the small repository-specific Node policy engine already in use.
Backstage offers broad software-governance/catalog capabilities but is far larger than the repository-local reuse-decision problem.
Git hooks remain useful for fast local pre-commit feedback but cannot enforce changes created directly through GitHub or other remote agents.

search_ladder.conclusion: Backstage covers broader software governance and cataloging, but its deployment and operating surface are disproportionate for one static-site repository.
OPA/Conftest can express the policy generically, but adds a second policy language/runtime where the existing Node gate already owns the repository-specific semantics.
GitHub Actions plus a PR-range-aware extension of the existing Node gate covers remote agents, clean runners, changed-file verification and required checks with minimal new machinery.
Git hooks and npm lifecycle scripts remain valuable as low-latency local feedback, but are supplemental because they cannot police GitHub-only changes.

candidates.name: Existing Node reuse gate extended with GitHub PR-range enforcement
candidates.license: Project code plus GitHub hosted CI
candidates.reason: Extends the already-proven gate into the clean CI environment, reuses Git and Actions, and keeps the policy implementation small while adding machine-verifiable PR coverage.

candidates.name: OPA / Conftest policy engine
candidates.reason: Technically capable but introduces Rego, a new binary/toolchain and duplicate policy ownership without providing enough additional value for this repository-sized policy.

candidates.name: Backstage Software Catalog and governance surface
candidates.reason: Provides far broader governance than needed and would introduce a service-sized operational dependency for a single repository reuse policy.

candidates.name: Git hooks and npm lifecycle only
candidates.reason: Keep as fast local feedback, but it cannot enforce GitHub connector edits, cloud agents or PRs created without the local checkout.

coverage_matrix.decision: Use the existing Node gate in GitHub Actions because it gives full PR-range enforcement without adding a second policy runtime.

coverage_matrix.capability: Parallel agents with independent task approvals
coverage_matrix.decision: Add task-scoped record and approval files so independent branches and agents do not contend on one global current/approval token.

coverage_matrix.capability: Protection of the gate and CI policy itself
coverage_matrix.decision: Treat workflow and gate policy paths as protected implementation and require architecture-level policy_change approval for modifications.
Retain Git hooks and npm lifecycle checks as a complementary fast path while GitHub remains the authoritative merge gate.

decision.rationale: Extend the existing repository-local Node gate and execute it against GitHub PR commit ranges. This preserves the current reuse semantics, adds machine-verifiable cloud enforcement, supports concurrent task approvals, and avoids introducing a second generic policy platform.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: Backstage is broader than the selected subsystem but its service deployment, plugin model and operational surface add substantially more cost than the narrow repository policy requires.

OPA is a stronger generic policy framework, but the existing Node gate already encodes the required semantics; adding Rego would duplicate policy ownership and slow iteration without improving current coverage.

decision.fallback: If the repository policy outgrows the Node implementation materially, migrate the validated structured records to OPA/Conftest rather than adding more ad-hoc shell checks.
